products.name: QIDI Q2 Enclosed CoreXY 3D Printer, 65 °C active chamber heating, 370 °C nozzle, 270 × 270 × 256 mm
specs: 56 dB printing, measured by a reviewer; 65 dB with the QIDI Box attached
Optional QIDI Box (sold separately or as the Q2 Combo)
products.warranty: 1 year from the date you receive the printer under QIDI's warranty statement; consumables such as nozzles, hotends and build plates are excluded.
products.returns: QIDI web store: no-reason returns within 14 days of receipt per its return policy page; used or incomplete returns may be refunded only in part, and the buyer pays return shipping if no fault is found. Confirm the window at checkout.
products.summary: The cheapest enclosed printer with a real chamber heater. Its 65 °C chamber, 370 °C nozzle and 120 °C bed cover ABS, ASA, nylon and carbon-fiber blends that passive enclosures like the Bambu P1S struggle with on larger parts.
products.fit: Hobbyists and small shops whose main output is ABS, ASA or nylon parts up to about 10.5 inches square, on a budget under $500.
caveats: PLA needs the lid and door open: QIDI says keep the chamber at or below 45 °C for PLA, and reviewers who printed PLA closed up got heat-creep clogs.
The optional QIDI Box jammed repeatedly for Tom's Hardware and Thomas Sanladerer; buy the printer alone unless you need multi-color.
Louder than a Bambu P1S: one reviewer measured 56 dB printing, and the idle fan is audible.
The camera runs at 640 × 480 and the QIDI Link app is poorly rated; the stock slicer profiles need tuning for PETG overhangs.

products.name: QIDI Plus5 Enclosed CoreXY 3D Printer, 65 °C active chamber heating, 370 °C nozzle, 320 × 320 × 300 mm
specs: CoreXY with linear guide rail on X and 9 mm 1.5GT belts
Load cell built into the hotend
48 dB in normal use, measured by a reviewer
products.warranty: 1 year from the date you receive the printer under QIDI's warranty statement; consumables such as nozzles, hotends and build plates are excluded.
products.returns: QIDI web store: no-reason returns within 14 days of receipt per its return policy page; used or incomplete returns may be refunded only in part, and the buyer pays return shipping if no fault is found. Confirm the window at checkout.
products.summary: The successor to the Plus 4 adds 18 percent more build volume, a 550 W chamber heater and load-cell leveling. For ABS and ASA parts over 10 inches it is the least expensive printer with a 65 °C chamber.
products.fit: Makers printing large ABS, ASA, PC or nylon parts, such as helmets, enclosures and brackets up to 12.6 inches square, who do not need Bambu-style multi-color.
caveats: Print PLA and TPU with the lid and door open; the insulated chamber causes heat-creep clogs otherwise.

The predecessor Plus 4 had owner fire reports tied to the chamber-heater relay in late 2024 and 2025; QIDI shipped replacement relays. The Plus5 uses a new heater design, but we found no independent safety test of it.
Multi-color needs the separate QIDI Box, which reviewers found unreliable on the Q2.
A 64 lb printer: plan for a sturdy table.

specs: CoreXY with closed-loop steppers and 2 mm lead Z screws
products.warranty: 1 year from the date you receive the printer under QIDI's warranty statement; consumables such as nozzles, hotends and build plates are excluded.
products.returns: QIDI web store: no-reason returns within 14 days of receipt per its return policy page; used or incomplete returns may be refunded only in part, and the buyer pays return shipping if no fault is found. Confirm the window at checkout.
products.summary: The biggest heated-chamber printer under $1,100. A 15.4-inch-square bed with a 65 °C chamber and 370 °C nozzle handles full-size ABS and nylon parts that the Plus5 and Creality K2 Plus cannot fit.
products.fit: Shops that need ABS, ASA or nylon parts over 12.6 inches, or want to print several large parts per plate.
caveats: Early owners reported firmware and extruder problems after updates; back up settings before flashing.
PLA clogs from heat creep if the chamber stays warm; QIDI sells a $199 Polar Cooler as the fix.
At 103 lb it is a two-person lift.
QIDI's own comparison lists it at $1,049; we could not confirm a higher regular price.
